money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Euro. Latvia is a member of the European Union (EU). If you're travelling between Latvia and any non-EU country, you must declare amounts over 10,000 euros or equivalent. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You'll have to pay a fine when you enter or leave Latvia if you: don't declare this money give incorrect information You don't need to declare currency if you're travelling between EU countries.

laws.rule: Travelling overseas can be stressful and uncertain. You may experience unfamiliar environments, travel disruptions, changes in normal routines and limited access to health care. Not taking your prescribed medications is a common cause of mental ill-health for Australians overseas. If you are concerned about your welfare, or someone else's, contact your nearest Australian embassy, high commission, or consulate. You can also call the 24-hour Consular Emergency Centre on [see source]. Mental health resources:
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: If you plan to drive in Latvia, you're required to obtain an International Driving Permit (IDP). Get your IDP before you leave Australia. You should also carry your Australian driver's licence (digital licences may not be accepted).
laws.heading: International Driving Permit

laws.rule: Anyone entering or leaving the European Union with cash worth EUR 10,000 or more (about A$15,900 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293) must declare it to customs. Cash here means banknotes and coins, bearer cheques and similar instruments, gold and other commodities used as stores of value, and prepaid cards. Each member state sets its own penalty for not declaring; the EU regulation says penalties must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
laws.heading: Cash declaration (EU Regulation 2018/1672)

laws.rule: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU duty-free allowance is 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus one of: 1 litre of spirits over 22% alcohol, or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine. The EU page tells travellers to check the destination country's customs for the latest limits.
laws.heading: Duty-free alcohol from outside the EU

laws.rule: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU allowance is 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco. The EU page says a lower limit (40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of tobacco) applies to land and sea travellers in some EU countries; check this country's customs. You can mix product types but the total must stay within the limit.
laws.heading: Duty-free tobacco from outside the EU

laws.rule: Travelling into the EU from a non-EU country, you are not allowed to bring any meat or dairy products. Limited amounts of fruit and vegetables, eggs, egg products, honey and some fish are allowed. Exceptions: up to 10 kg per person from the Faroe Islands or Greenland, and up to 2 kg of powdered infant milk, infant food or special medical foods (unopened, shelf-stable, proprietary brand), or health-related pet food for an accompanying pet. Undeclared products are confiscated and destroyed, and a fine or prosecution is possible.
laws.heading: Meat and dairy from outside the EU

laws.rule: Under Article 75 of the Schengen Convention, a traveller carrying narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances for their own medical treatment must be able to produce, at a check, a certificate issued or authenticated by a competent authority of their state of residence. The certificate form covers the substance, quantity and length of the journey. How a resident of Australia obtains one is not checked in this entry; ask this country's embassy or health authority before travel.
laws.heading: Schengen certificate for narcotic or psychotropic medicines (Article 75)

laws.rule: Gauja National Park (across Sigulda, Cēsis, Smiltene and other municipalities) is governed by the Gauja National Park Law. It bans moving on rivers, lakes and other water bodies in engine-powered craft, with exceptions for officials on duty and for Lake Ungurs (where the park agency's written permit is needed), bans damaging specially protected trees, and bans dumping waste outside landfills. In the nature reserve zone it also bans clear felling and burning dry grass and reeds, and the agency may close areas seasonally. Camping and fire rules are in Cabinet regulations that were not read in this check.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Latvia is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Hold a valid health insurance policy covering health-related expenses (required to enter).

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

The Civil Aviation Agency (CAA) registers operators and requires a verified account in its UASIS system for exams, cross-border applications and applications in UAS geographical zones. Latvian registration is valid for one year.
In UASIS an operator registered in another EEA country or Switzerland picks a separate option and supplies the requested information.

The CAA says drone users must check restrictions before each flight on the zone map at airspace.lv/drones, because they can change several times a day. Since 1 January 2025 applications to fly in any UAS geographical zone go through the CAA system (e.caa.gov.lv).
